sections.h2: What does the Robeson County Register of Deeds do when you sell a house?
sections.html:
It records the deed that moves title from you to your buyer, along with the buyer's deed of trust, any release of your old loan and the plats and other land papers for Robeson County. The office is in Lumberton and takes a phone line of 910-671-3040 for recording questions.

Staff may not prepare deeds or give legal advice. The county's recording page says state statute forbids it, and that the office has no forms. For any question about what a document should say, the answer is to see an attorney.

A conveyance only gains priority over lien creditors and later buyers for value from the time it is registered in the county where the land is, as G.S. 47-18 sets out.

sections.h2: Why does a Robeson County deed need tax certification before recording?
sections.html:
The Robeson County register's recording page says all deeds require tax certification before recording, or else the delinquent tax statement described in G.S. 161-31. Without one of them, a deed mailed to the office is sent back to the sender.

This step catches many first-time sellers. It comes before the deed ever reaches the recording counter, and it runs through the county tax department, not the register.

  • Email the document to the tax office at deeds@robesoncountync.gov, or
  • Mail it to the Robeson County Tax Department, 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton NC 28358, or
  • Call the tax office at 910-671-3060 for instructions.

Build this stop into your timeline, and ask your closing attorney whether the firm already requests certifications as routine practice.

sections.h2: What other rules apply to recording in person or by mail in Robeson County?
sections.html:
Any document recorded in person must carry a return name and mailing address. If you do not provide a self-addressed stamped envelope, the office charges a $1.00 mailing fee.

Before anything is recorded the paper has to be prepared, signed and notarized. The office cannot fix a defective acknowledgment or fill in missing terms for you.

If you mail a deed, include the tax certification or delinquent tax statement from the start, since a package without it comes back. Phone the register at 910-671-3040 with questions about a specific filing. The county's online records tools also let anyone search deed information from a computer.

sections.h2: What does the Robeson County Register of Deeds charge to record?
sections.html:
Recording fees come from the uniform state schedule in G.S. 161-10, which is the same in every county. Ask the register about accepted payment types and any extra charges such as the mailing fee described above.

State recording fees that apply in Robeson County
ItemFee
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 per added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Each extra instrument inside one filing adds $10.00, and the fees are due before filing.

sections.h2: How much is the excise tax on a Robeson County deed?
sections.html:
The tax is $1.00 for each $500, or fraction of $500, of the price or value conveyed, under G.S. 105-228.30. The seller, called the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before recording.

The register keeps half for the county general fund and sends the state half on to the Department of Revenue each month, after refunds, and a county may keep 2 percent of the state share. For a parcel in more than one county, the one with the greater value collects.

Your closing attorney will show the figure on the settlement statement. If you want a quote beforehand, give the office the sale price and ask.

sections.h2: What property tax details matter on a Robeson County closing?
sections.html:
Tax liability for the year stays with the owner on January 1, and a sale during the year does not erase the seller's liability, according to the Robeson County tax office. Taxes are usually prorated at closing as a private arrangement between buyer and seller.

If you want to be sure no bill is left behind, you can ask to pay the tax collector at closing. When the current-year bill is not yet due, the county accepts prepayment based on the prior year's rate. Both names may be advertised for past-due taxes if the property sold during the year and the bill went unpaid.

The same tax office certifies the deed before recording, so one phone call often covers both topics.

sections.h2: What other documents might a Robeson County seller record?
sections.html:
Besides the deed, a recorded satisfaction clears your mortgage, and no fee applies to that filing. An option, a contract to convey, or a lease over three years must be registered to bind later buyers and lien creditors. A contract for deed under Chapter 47H must be recorded, or a memorandum of it, within five business days.

  • Check that your payoff produces a recorded satisfaction.
  • Keep a copy of every recorded paper.
  • Ask the attorney whether a plat or easement affects the lot.

faqs.q: Does the Robeson County Register of Deeds give legal advice?
faqs.a: No. The county says state statute prohibits the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds. It also has no forms, so consult an attorney.

faqs.q: What happens if I mail a deed without tax certification?
faqs.a: It is returned to the sender. Robeson County requires tax certification or the delinquent tax statement before a deed can be recorded.

faqs.q: How do I get tax certification on a Robeson County deed?
faqs.a: Email the document to deeds@robesoncountync.gov, mail it to the Robeson County Tax Department at 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton, or call 910-671-3060.

faqs.q: Is there a mailing fee for recorded documents in Robeson County?
faqs.a: Yes, $1.00, if you record in person and do not give a self-addressed stamped envelope. Every in-person filing must carry a return name and address.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Robeson County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays the $1.00 per $500 tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Your closing attorney normally collects it at closing.
